item.title: Trump announces "crushing economic operation" on Iran with talks in limbo
item.description: President Trump said Wednesday the U.S. might return to negotiations with Iran eventually, but he said currently "the situation is so good."

item.title: One killed when small plane, state police helicopter collide in Pennsylvania
item.description: One person was killed and two Pennsylvania State Police troopers were injured when a small plane and a state police helicopter were involved in a midair collision in central Pennsylvania, authorities said.

item.title: Pentagon officials considering firing Stars and Stripes publisher, sources say
item.description: Max Lederer, who has served as the publisher of Stars and Stripes for 19 years, this week announced to colleagues his decision to retire on Sept. 30, citing fundamental differences with the Trump administration.

item.title: Thousands still without power in Indiana more than a week after storm
item.description: Over a week after a storm knocked out power to several towns in Indiana, thousands are still living without electricity and struggling to get warm meals. CBS News Chicago's Sabrina Franza reports.

item.title: How Moderna's melanoma mRNA vaccine could fight deadliest skin cancer
item.description: CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder, who has had melanoma herself, said Moderna's experimental trial is "a big win for mRNA vaccines against cancer."

item.title: Inside the investigation into Mark Walter amid his sale of the Los Angeles Lakers
item.description: Billionaire Mark Walter moved to sell the Los Angeles Lakers last week for a record $12.5 billion just 14 months after purchasing the team as he faces a federal investigation. Melody Gutierrez, senior investigative reporter at The Athletic, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Army unit offers 4-day passes to play Grand Theft Auto VI to encourage reenlistments
item.description: A U.S. Army unit based in Georgia is offering soldiers four days of leave to play Grand Theft Auto IV when it's released in November as a way to incentivize reenlistments. CBS News Pentagon reporter Eleanor Watson has more.

item.title: Trump pauses border wall construction in Texas' Big Bend National Park amid Abbott pushback
item.description: President Trump is pausing construction of a border wall in Texas' Big Bend National Park after bipartisan concerns about its impact on the natural landscape, CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott announced. CBS News' Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: Moderna reaches "landmark moment" in Melanoma vaccine trial
item.description: CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder joins "The Daily Report" to discuss what Moderna's melanoma vaccine breakthrough could mean as clinical trials continue.

item.title: Senate races set in Alaska and Florida as midterms approach, could determine chamber control
item.description: Senate races are now set in Alaska and Florida as midterm elections approach. The Florida race turned on its head after an upset primary win by Angie Nixon, a democratic socialist. CBS News' Zak Hudak reports.

item.title: Woman told House panel that Gomez sexually assaulted her, attorneys say
item.description: The California Democrat said Monday that he "made personal mistakes outside my marriage" and that his "actions were consensual in nature."

item.title: 5 Americans among 7 people killed in Kenya helicopter crash
item.description: NBCUniversal said its Florida-based journalist, José Alberto Suárez, who worked for CBS Miami in the 1990s, was among those killed in the crash.

item.title: Strategists say Angie Nixon, DSA candidates will hurt Democrats in general elections
item.description: Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon, a democratic socialist candidate, pulled off an upset victory Tuesday over a more moderate opponent to win the Democratic nomination in her Florida Senate race. Democratic strategist Matt Bennett and Republican strategist Mike Hahn join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: What to know about Mark Walter, owner of Dodgers and Lakers, as he faces federal probe
item.description: Mark Walter's sports empire appears to be crumbling due to a federal investigation he's facing. Ben Horney, deals reporter at Front Office Sports, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: 47-year-old father walks onto San Jose City College football team: "Joy of the game"
item.description: A 47-year-old father of three walked onto the San Jose City College football team this year. He is taking a beating, but is loving it, and spoke with Tony Dokoupil about the experience.

item.title: Pennsylvania gubernatorial candidate Stacy Garrity on data centers, calls for construction pause
item.description: Pennsylvania Republican gubernatorial candidate Stacy Garrity joins "The Takeout" to discuss why she wants a pause on data center construction, even as President Trump calls for more to be built.

item.title: Massachusetts police searching for wife of cop found dead at home
item.description: Police in Massachusetts are looking for Karen Solomon, a woman whose husband was found dead at their home. Police have said she is "presumed to be armed and dangerous." CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Moderna stock surges as melanoma vaccine trial shows "landmark moment"
item.description: Moderna and Merck announced study results that reflect a "landmark moment" in treatment for one of the deadliest forms of skin cancer.

item.title: Prince Harry and Meghan moving back to U.K.
item.description: The couple said in January 2020 that they would be stepping away from "senior" royal roles​ and were working to become financially independent from the royal family.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy testimony ends early due to "unforeseen circumstance"
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial continued Wednesday in Massachusetts, though testimony for the day ended earlier than expected.

item.title: 8/19: CBS Evening News
item.description: 5 Americans were killed in a tourist helicopter crash in Kenya; nearly 100 million in the U.S. felt the heat coast-to-coast.

item.title: Some pool owners renting out access through Swimply: "I'll probably look to make about $15,000"
item.description: The cost of building a backyard pool has climbed out of reach for many, but in the heat of summer, there's no better place to cool off. With that in mind, more people are renting access to pools at private homes. Bradley Blackburn dives in and explains.

item.title: Penn State frat brothers charged with running cocaine trafficking ring
item.description: Two Penn State fraternities are at the center of a cocaine trafficking ring bust, leading to charges against 14 people, authorities said.

item.title: Doctors urge student vaccinations as preventable diseases like the measles rise
item.description: With vaccine-preventable diseases like the measles are on the rise in the U.S., pediatricians are encouraging students to stay up to date on their vaccines before the school year starts. CBS News' Jarred Hill reports on what doctors want parents to know.

item.title: 8/19: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Angie Nixon pulls off upset win in Florida primary; Trump says peace talks with Iran will resume "maybe at some point."

item.title: National debt tops $40 trillion after doubling in under 10 years
item.description: Federal debt has mounted amid tax cuts and trillions in pandemic spending, adding to the nation's interest payments.

item.title: Trump pausing 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods as deal being finalized
item.description: President Trump said Tuesday that the U.S. and Canada have reached a last-minute agreement to pause the 50% tariffs.

item.title: Army unit offers 4-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto as reenlistment incentive
item.description: Eligible soldiers must reenlist for a minimum of two years and up to six years.

item.title: Moving pillowcase leads to discovery of reptiles in car seized at border
item.description: Federal officers found a moving pillowcase in a car that was seized at the U.S.-Mexico border. A collection of stolen exotic reptiles was inside.

item.title: School vaccination rates decline again as exemptions reach new high
item.description: U.S. kindergarten vaccination rates have declined again, with exemptions reaching a record high for the 2025-2026 school year
